extra_quotes: All analytical evaluations in this paper use the single parameter set of Table 3 [51-53] (Si, 300 K; asymmetric p+–n junction).
(i) SCR generation–recombination is neglected in the closure (Sec. VI A), as in the classical theory
(ii) Frozen ambipolar coefficients : the closed form pairs the exact, injection -dependent boundary excess with transport coefficients evaluated at their low -injection limits.

(iii) Neglected ambipolar drift: the perturbative elimination of 𝜇𝜇𝑎𝑎𝐸𝐸 𝑑𝑑𝛿𝛿/𝑑𝑑𝑥𝑥 (Sec. III A) is bounded in closed form: the associated ambipolar Péclet number satisfies |Pe𝑎𝑎| ≤ 1/4(𝑏𝑏 + 1) ≈ 6% for Si, peaking at 𝛿𝛿0 ≈ 0.75 𝑛𝑛0 and vanishing in both injection limits (Appendix A)

(iv) Constant material parameters: bias -independent 𝜇𝜇 and 𝜏𝜏 are used throughout; at the highest injections, mobility degradation, Auger recombination, and self-heating (neglected here) would increase the base drops, so the ohmic drop reported in Sec. VII is a lower bound to what a fully coupled electro- thermal model would give [8,9,41].

(v) Structure idealization : uniformly doped, abrupt, one -dimensional junctions are assumed; graded bases, heterojunctions, and two-dimensional effects are outside the present scope, as are organic and disordered semiconductors, for which the dielectric- relaxation bound of Sec. II would have to be re-examined.
